clinicalPearls: Inflammatory myopathy arising alongside another defined connective tissue disease, or defined by an overlap-associated autoantibody, rather than as isolated myositis.
The antisynthetase syndrome is a key subset, marked by anti-Jo-1 or other anti-tRNA-synthetase antibodies (anti-PL-7, anti-PL-12, anti-EJ, anti-OJ, anti-KS).
Its clinical cluster comprises myositis, interstitial lung disease, non-erosive arthritis, Raynaud phenomenon, mechanic's hands and fever, though not all features are present together.
Anti-PM/Scl antibodies define a scleroderma-myositis overlap with sclerodactyly, Raynaud and calcinosis, and generally carry a favourable, steroid-responsive course.
Anti-U1-RNP points to mixed connective tissue disease, while anti-Ku indicates another overlap phenotype.
Muscle weakness is often milder than in classic polymyositis or dermatomyositis, and creatine kinase may be only modestly raised.
Interstitial lung disease is the principal driver of morbidity and mortality and can be the presenting or dominant feature.
There is a female predominance and a chronic relapsing course requiring long-term immunosuppression.
reference.pathophysiology: Overlap myositis is an autoimmune inflammatory myopathy that occurs within the immune dysregulation of a broader connective tissue disease and is closely linked to specific autoantibodies. In the antisynthetase syndrome, antibodies target aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases, and it is proposed that these enzymes, upregulated and exposed in regenerating muscle and injured lung epithelium, act as autoantigens that sustain a self-amplifying response involving both antibody and T-cell mechanisms. Anti-PM/Scl and anti-U1-RNP overlaps share features of scleroderma and lupus-spectrum disease, with vasculopathy, complement activation and cytokine-driven fibrosis contributing to the muscle, skin and lung manifestations.
additionalInvestigations: Serum creatine kinase and muscle enzymes
Extended myositis and overlap antibody panel (anti-Jo-1 and other synthetases, anti-PM/Scl, anti-U1-RNP, anti-Ku)
High-resolution CT of the chest and pulmonary function tests with gas transfer
Electromyography and muscle MRI or biopsy
Echocardiography to assess for pulmonary hypertension
redFlags: Progressive breathlessness or rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease
reference.prognosis: Outcome is variable and largely determined by the presence and severity of interstitial lung disease; anti-PM/Scl overlap is relatively favourable, whereas some antisynthetase phenotypes carry a poorer prognosis. The disease typically follows a chronic relapsing course needing sustained immunosuppression.
pitfalls: Overlooking interstitial lung disease, which may dominate the presentation while muscle symptoms are mild.
Attributing arthritis solely to rheumatoid disease and missing the overlap.
Missing overlap antibodies when only a limited myositis panel is requested.
Underestimating disease when creatine kinase is normal or only mildly elevated.
Failing to reassess for pulmonary hypertension over time.
references: EULAR/ACR classification criteria for idiopathic inflammatory myopathies
European Neuromuscular Centre (ENMC) workshop reports on antisynthetase and overlap myositis
management: Induce disease control with corticosteroids as first-line immunosuppression for the inflammatory myopathy
Add a steroid-sparing immunosuppressant such as methotrexate, azathioprine or mycophenolate mofetil for maintenance and to limit steroid toxicity
Treat significant interstitial lung disease more aggressively with agents such as mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide or rituximab, since lung involvement drives prognosis
Use intravenous immunoglobulin for refractory or severe myositis
Manage Raynaud phenomenon with cold avoidance and a calcium-channel blocker, and provide physiotherapy and skin care for mechanic's hands and arthritis
Monitor creatine kinase, pulmonary function with gas transfer, and high-resolution CT to track myositis and lung-disease activity
Coordinate rheumatology, respiratory and physiotherapy input, escalating for rapidly progressive interstitial lung disease or respiratory compromise
